title: Valentine's Weekend City Breaks from UK Airports: Flights from £34
subtitle: Lisbon and Seville from £34 one-way beat Paris and Venice on value every time
airport_names: London Stansted, Gatwick, Heathrow, Luton, Manchester, Edinburgh
meta: Valentine's city breaks from UK airports: Lisbon from £34, Seville from £39, Rome from £29 one-way. Honest verdicts on Paris, Venice, Vienna and Copenhagen.

sections.heading: The cheap ones: Lisbon, Seville and Rome
sections.body:
Lisbon from £34 one-way on Ryanair from Stansted is the best-value romantic flight I know of for mid-February. easyJet from Gatwick runs £39-£72 one-way, and TAP Air Portugal from Heathrow sits around £58-£95 if you want a free bag included. Daytime temperatures hover around 15C, which is jumper-and-scarf weather rather than shivering.

Seville from £39 one-way on easyJet from Gatwick is the other one to book. Ryanair also flies from Stansted at £31-£67 one-way, and I've seen it dip to £29 midweek. February is orange blossom season there, so the streets smell better than any candle you could buy.

Rome from £29 one-way on Ryanair from Stansted is the cheapest flight on this list. easyJet from Gatwick runs £36-£70, and British Airways from Heathrow starts around £65. The catch is that restaurant prices in the centre jump on 14 February, so book dinner early or eat out on the Friday instead.

sections.heading: The pricey ones: Paris, Venice and Vienna
sections.body:
Paris from £42 one-way on easyJet from Gatwick looks cheap until you check the hotels. Eurostar from St Pancras starts around £69 each way if you book early, but Valentine's weekend rooms in the 1st to 8th arrondissements regularly hit £200-£300 a night. It still delivers. Just stay in the 11th or 18th and walk.

Venice from £37 one-way on Ryanair from Stansted gets you to Treviso, about 40 minutes from the city by bus. Flights into Marco Polo on easyJet from Gatwick run £48-£95. Hotels in the city proper are eye-watering that weekend, so most couples I know stay in Mestre for under £90 a night and take the 10-minute train in.

Vienna from £45 one-way on Ryanair from Stansted is decent value, and Austrian Airlines from Heathrow runs £79-£130. The city is gorgeous in winter, with coffee houses, opera and Christmas market leftovers. Good flights, but accommodation is the sting, with central doubles around £150-£220 that weekend.

sections.heading: Copenhagen: romantic if you can stomach the prices
sections.body:
Copenhagen from £48 one-way on easyJet from Gatwick is the dearest flight here, with Norwegian and SAS from Heathrow typically £70-£120. Mid-February is cold, usually 2-5C, but that is the point. Candlelit cafes, canal walks and cinnamon buns in a bakery at 9am is peak hygge.

The honest bit is that Denmark is expensive. A modest dinner for two costs £70-£100, and a hotel double in the centre starts around £140. Couples I know keep costs down with a self-catering flat in Nørrebro or Vesterbro and a Copenhagen Card for transport.

Worth it if you want cosy over sunny. Skip it if your budget is tight, because Lisbon gives you a better weekend for roughly half the cost.

sections.heading: Keeping a couples' weekend affordable
sections.body:
A self-catering apartment beats a hotel almost every time in February. Lisbon one-beds in Alfama or Príncipe Real run £65-£95 a night, against £120-£180 for a comparable hotel. You also get a kitchen for breakfast, which saves £15-£20 a day. Book at least six weeks out, ideally now, because the good ones go by December.

The best romantic things in these cities cost nothing. Sunset at Miradouro da Senhora do Monte in Lisbon, a walk along the Guadalquivir in Seville, Rome's Spanish Steps at dusk, Paris from the steps of Sacré-Cœur. Pack a bottle of wine from a supermarket at £6-£8 and you've sorted the evening.

Book flights on a Thursday evening or Friday morning to save around £10-£25 per person against Friday departures. Add a cabin bag only if you need it, since Ryanair charges £10-£30 depending on timing. If you can fly Thursday and back Sunday, you will often pay less than the Friday-Monday crowd. Valentine's Day 2027 falls on a Sunday, so the weekend before is cheaper than the weekend itself.
